# Codanākaṇḍa (Pvr 13)

**ID:** Pvr 13
**Section:** Parivāra (pvr)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Codanākaṇḍa
**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** Accusations and the process of investigation

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Codanākaṇḍa* ("Chapter on Accusation") is the thirteenth section of the *Parivāra*, the final division of the Vinaya Piṭaka (Pvr 13; designated as Chapter XI in I. B. Horner's translation) [Horner, Book of the Discipline; SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral translates the title as "Accusations and the process of investigation" and characterizes the chapter as an analysis of the conditions and circumstances to be weighed when admonishing or reproving someone [SuttaCentral]. Modern English translations have been produced by I. B. Horner and Bhikkhu Brahmali [Horner, Book of the Discipline; SuttaCentral].

The text focuses primarily on the reprover (*codaka*) and the formal judicial investigation conducted by an ecclesiastical adjudicator [Horner, Book of the Discipline]. When a monk initiates an accusation, the adjudicator questions him to establish whether the alleged offense constitutes a lapse in moral habit (*sīlavipatti*), proper conduct (*ācāravipatti*), or right view (*diṭṭhivipatti*) [Horner, Book of the Discipline]. The treatise provides formal evidentiary tests for investigating allegations, examining whether statements based on what was seen, heard, or suspected agree and support one another [Entrance to the Vinaya 1983]. It also warns against the grave consequences of unskilled and incompetent reprovers, observing that abusive or groundless accusations against elders result in spiritual injury and rebirth in hell (*niraya*) [Horner, Book of the Discipline].

According to DharmaNexus, the *Codanākaṇḍa* shares substantial textual material across the Pali canon (527 matching passages across 25 texts) [DharmaNexus]. Its most extensive reuse occurs with the *Pavāraṇākkhandhaka* (Kd 4, particularly §1.1–1.37 aligned with Kd 16.10–16.15) and the *Mahāsaṅgāma* (Pvr 15), with further parallels in the *Samathakkhandhaka* (Kd 14), *Pātimokkhaṭṭhapanakkhandhaka* (Kd 19), *Upālipañcaka* (Pvr 17), the *Kakacūpama Sutta* (MN 21), and the *Pañcakanipāta* of the Aṅguttara Nikāya (AN 5.167) [DharmaNexus]. Passages are also extensively cited and discussed in Vinaya commentaries and sub-commentaries, including the *Vinayasaṅgaha-aṭṭhakathā*, *Vinayālaṅkāra-ṭīkā*, and *Parivāra-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. Beyond Pali, DharmaNexus identifies machine alignments with the Chinese *Saṃyuktāgama* (T 99) and Tibetan Vinaya works including the *Vinayavastu* (D 1) and *Vinaya-uttaragrantha* (D 7) [DharmaNexus].
